suggestions.reason: Trivially satisfied: this 495-word, six-header baseline passes because its scaffold is named What/Why/Changes instead of Overview/Summary. Tighten to 'no markdown section headers' or 'no generic scaffold headers (What, Why, Overview, Summary, Changes, Background)' so the assertion actually separates the two runs.

No assertion covers fabricated specifics. The baseline invented the content of the four tests and a motivating incident (lost events on transient 5xx) that appears nowhere in the inputs, and presented both as fact in the PR description. An assertion like 'every concrete claim traces to changes.md or the source tree' would catch this.

No assertion covers meta-commentary in the reply. The baseline opens with a paragraph about the executor's working tree ('the working tree I have only contains...') before the description, which a reviewer-facing PR description should never carry. check.py's apology_or_meta regex did not catch it.

eval_feedback.overall: Two of five assertions pass; the 'No Overview or Summary headers' pass is a false positive in spirit, since the output uses an equivalent What/Why/Changes scaffold. The uncaught problems are invented details (test cases, motivation) stated as fact.
